title: $1,000 now or $1,200 later?
hook: $1,200 is more than $1,000. Is it worth more, if you have to wait?

knows: compounding: money earning a rate grows each year (compound-interest lesson)
doesNotKnow: that money later is worth less today, because money now could be earning
that which offer is better depends on the rate you could earn

misconception: $1,200 later is obviously more than $1,000 now.
objective: The learner can explain that a future amount is worth what it would take today to grow into it, so comparing offers at different times needs a rate, and the better offer can flip as the rate changes.

claims.text: At 5% a year, $1,200 in 3 years is worth $1,036.61 today, so it beats $1,000 now, by about $37.
A future amount is worth today what you would need now to grow into it at the rate you could earn.
claims.source: Present value = FV / (1 + r)^n (N. G. Mankiw, Principles of Economics, ch. 27, 'Present Value').

claims.text: At 7% the later offer is worth only $979.56 today, less than $1,000.
The answer flips above about 6.27% a year.
On the stage the later offer's value today ranges from $1,200 at 0% to $854 at 12%.
The lesson is a model: a sure payment, a steady rate, no tax; it is not advice.
claims.source: Assumptions of the lesson's own calculation, shown on the stage chip and in the reveal.

recall.question: You are offered $500 now or $550 in 2 years. You could earn 10% a year. Which is worth more today?
recall.why: $500 at 10% grows to $605 in 2 years, more than $550. Put the other way, $550 in 2 years is worth only about $455 today.
